newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr inches up vs yen but fails to hit high.
newsitem.headline: Dlr inches up vs yen but fails to hit high.

text.p: Dollar crept up vs yen in early Tokyo trading but failed to rise above 127.16 yen, its highest level since August 1992.
*Traders keen to sell dollars to avoid hitting knock-out options points at around 127.30 yen, weighing on dollar.
*Even if greenback rises above 127.30 yen, exporter offers expected near 127.50 yen are likely to limit its gains.
*On the downside, operators, including trust banks and investment trust firms, eager to buy dollars on any dips, keeping dollar solid.
*"The strong U.S. data, coupled with strong U.S. stocks, was bullish for the dollar," a trust bank dealer said, adding speed of dollar's rise may accelerate once it clearly breaks through 127.30 yen.
*He added that if Japanese investors decide to actively buy dollars, that would also give greenback a chance to rise further.
*A city bank dealer said the dollar is likely to be supported just below 1.73 marks during Asian trading time.
